variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: Uber ridesharing architecture is the real-time marketplace system that connects a rider request to one eligible nearby driver, then keeps both people synchronized through pickup, travel, payment, and completion. It combines rapidly expiring location data, geospatial search, dispatch decisions, pricing signals, and a durable trip state machine.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Driver location
pairs.detail: Store driver ID, coordinate or cell, observed time, availability epoch, product eligibility, heading, and expiry.
pairs.explanation: Store driver ID, coordinate or cell, observed time, availability epoch, product eligibility, heading, and expiry. A missing or expired coordinate means unknown, not nearby.

pairs.label: Driver offer
pairs.detail: Store offer ID, trip ID, driver ID, score snapshot, issue time, expiry, response, and reservation token.
pairs.explanation: Store offer ID, trip ID, driver ID, score snapshot, issue time, expiry, response, and reservation token. Expiry returns the candidate to search; it does not reassign the trip by itself.

pairs.label: Trip
pairs.detail: Store trip ID, rider, region owner, state, assigned driver, quote ID, monotonically increasing version, timestamps, and cancellation reason.
pairs.explanation: Store trip ID, rider, region owner, state, assigned driver, quote ID, monotonically increasing version, timestamps, and cancellation reason.

pairs.label: Command and outbox
pairs.detail: Store the idempotency key, expected trip version, result, event ID, schema version, and publication status so uncertain acknowledgements can be resolved safely.
pairs.explanation: Store the idempotency key, expected trip version, result, event ID, schema version, and publication status so uncertain acknowledgements can be resolved safely.

variants.hint:

pairs.label: Requested
pairs.detail: The rider command creates one regional trip identity.
pairs.explanation: The rider command creates one regional trip identity. Repeating the same command returns that identity.

pairs.label: Offered
pairs.detail: Dispatch can create several sequential or bounded parallel offers, but none is the assignment until trip authority commits it.
pairs.explanation: Dispatch can create several sequential or bounded parallel offers, but none is the assignment until trip authority commits it.

pairs.label: Assigned
pairs.detail: The first valid acceptance advances the expected trip version and records one driver.
pairs.explanation: The first valid acceptance advances the expected trip version and records one driver. Later acceptances fail cleanly.

pairs.label: Terminal
pairs.detail: Completion and cancellation are versioned transitions with durable events.
pairs.explanation: Completion and cancellation are versioned transitions with durable events. Consumers ignore stale or duplicate event versions.

pairs.label: Retrieve
pairs.detail: Read the pickup cell and neighbors, reject expired coordinates, and expand the radius only when fresh recall is below policy.
pairs.explanation: Read the pickup cell and neighbors, reject expired coordinates, and expand the radius only when fresh recall is below policy.

pairs.label: Filter and estimate
pairs.detail: Apply product, capacity, accessibility, compliance, availability-epoch, and reservation checks.
pairs.explanation: Apply product, capacity, accessibility, compliance, availability-epoch, and reservation checks. Estimate road ETA rather than straight-line distance alone.

pairs.label: Score and offer
pairs.detail: Balance pickup ETA, acceptance likelihood, driver idle time, destination preferences, fairness, and cancellation risk.
pairs.explanation: Balance pickup ETA, acceptance likelihood, driver idle time, destination preferences, fairness, and cancellation risk. Offer to a bounded set with an expiry.

pairs.label: Commit or expand
pairs.detail: Commit the accepted driver against the trip version.
pairs.explanation: Commit the accepted driver against the trip version. On decline or expiry, continue with remaining candidates or expand under the wait and capacity budget.

variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: Uber ridesharing architecture is the real-time marketplace system that connects a rider request to one eligible nearby driver, then keeps both people synchronized through pickup, travel, payment, and completion. It combines rapidly expiring location data, geospatial search, dispatch decisions, pricing signals, and a durable trip state machine.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: City-focused application
pairs.detail: A compact application and relational store can validate the marketplace quickly.
pairs.explanation: A compact application and relational store can validate the marketplace quickly. The main benefit is speed of change; the limit is coupling between location churn, trip writes, pricing, and city operations.

pairs.label: Domain services
pairs.detail: Location, dispatch, trip, pricing, and payments separate around distinct access patterns and ownership.
pairs.explanation: Location, dispatch, trip, pricing, and payments separate around distinct access patterns and ownership. The cost is explicit contracts, deployment coordination, and operational maturity.

pairs.label: Real-time event platform
pairs.detail: Durable streams decouple trip commits from analytics, notifications, safety, and support.
pairs.explanation: Durable streams decouple trip commits from analytics, notifications, safety, and support. Replay improves recovery but requires idempotent, version-aware consumers.

pairs.label: Regional and ML-assisted marketplace
pairs.detail: Regional isolation limits latency and blast radius while models improve ETA, matching, positioning, and pricing.
pairs.explanation: Regional isolation limits latency and blast radius while models improve ETA, matching, positioning, and pricing. Governance, fallback behavior, and feature freshness become first-class design work.
